chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn Abi Wahb al-Qasri, who said:

I entered Medina, so I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I came to you and I have not performed the Ziyarah of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Bad is what you have done. Had you not been from our Shiah, I would not have looked at you. Do you not visit the one whom Allah visits along with the Angels, and the Prophets visit him, and the believers visit him?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I had no knowledge of that.' He said: 'Know that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) is superior in the Presence of Allah than all the Imams, and for him is the reward of their deeds, and they are distinguished according to the measure of their deeds.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting Imam Ali (AS) according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the narrator’s assumption that visiting the Prophet suffices, elevating the Ziyarah of Imam Ali (AS) as a prerequisite for true Shia identity. The text establishes a unique theological hierarchy where Imam Ali (AS) is superior to all other Imams, possessing the cumulative reward of their collective deeds, a concept central to Shia understanding of the Imamate's spiritual authority. This underscores the practical implication that honoring the Commander of the Faithful is essential for accessing the merits of the entire Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Hamdan Bin Suleyman, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Yamani, from Mani’e Bin Al Hajjaj, from Yunus Bin Abu Wahab Al Qasry who said,

‘I entered Al-Medina, so I went to Abu Abdullahasws and I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! I came to youasws and I have not performed the Ziyarah of Amir Al-Momineenasws’. Heasws said: ‘Iasws am unhappy with what you have done, and had you not being from ourasws Shiah, Iasws would not have even looked at you. You did not visit the oneasws whom Allahazwj visits along with the Angels, and the Prophetsas visit himasws, and the believers visit himasws?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! I had no knowledge of that’. Heasws said: ‘Know that Amir Al-Momineenasws is superior in the Presence of Allahazwj than the Imamsasws, all of themasws, and for himasws is the Reward of theirasws deeds, and upon a measurement of theirasws deeds having merits’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Hamdan ibn Sulayman from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Yemaniy from Mani‘ ibn al- Hajjaj from Yunus ibn Wahab al-Qasriy who has said the following:

“I once entered al-Madinah, visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said to him, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I have come to you but I have not visited ’Amir al- Mu’minin.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You have done a bad thing. Were you not one of our followers, I would not have looked at you. Why should you not visit one whom Allah along with the angels visit, the prophets and believers visit?’ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I did not know that.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must take notice that ’Amir al-Mu’minin is more excellent before Allah than all of ’A’immah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam. For him is the reward for their deeds and the degree of excellence is according to the measure of their deeds.’”
